judge.one_line: The demonstration vocabulary is genuinely good — unit blocks, area circles, a tipping scale — but seg1 shows 2000-vs-2012 at 33% while the voice says 92% by 2023, and the last six frames ship clipped and overlapping text.
problems: seg1:mid / seg1:end: bars labeled '2000 VS 2012' with 33% on the right and no value on the 2000 bar, directly contradicting the narration 'was over 92%' printed on the same frame.
seg4:start through payoff@-0.4: the right pan label is truncated to 'Staffed checkou' — cut off by the frame edge in all six final frames.
payoff@-1.8, seg4:end, payoff@-0.4: the 'COMMENT BELOW ▼' CTA is drawn directly on top of the four-line source citation, rendering both into unreadable mush at the bottom of the screen.
seg3:start / seg3:mid: the source line is clipped on the LEFT edge ('ail Federation (NRF)...') and runs off the right edge.

seg2:start (t=17.66s) shows a balance scale reading 3.1M / 2.7M while seg2:mid and seg2:end show a line chart — two different machines inside one segment, and the scale's numbers never reach the narrated 3.5M / 3.0M.
hook@0.3 to seg0:end: composition wastes the bottom third; the block stack is roughly one-third of frame width with the mascot tiny on top, reading as amateur layout rather than a designed frame.
fixes: Re-source seg1 from the endpoints the script states: 2000 = 6%, 2023 = 92%, header 'self-checkout adoption, 2000 vs 2023', and always render a value label on the baseline bar — a comparison machine with an unlabeled bar must refuse rather than draw.
Constrain pan labels on the balance machine to the pan's horizontal extent (shrink-to-fit or wrap 'Staffed\ncheckout') so nothing crosses the safe area — currently truncated in every seg4 frame.
Reserve a bottom band for the source citation and place the CTA above it; never composite CTA and sources into the same rows as at payoff@-0.4.
Left-align source text inside the card's padding so it cannot clip off either edge (seg3:start).
Hold one machine per segment: either the scale or the line chart for seg2, and make the counters land on 3.5M and 3.0M to match the narration.

Scale the hook stack to fill the frame width and drop the baseline lower so the bottom third carries the stack instead of empty gradient; make the mascot's reaction to the stack topping out the hook's action beat.

rules: TITLE or HOOK must contain a consequential NUMBER from the data below (the gate refuses a title+hook with no digit in either).

TITLE must be a PREMISE, not a searchable noun phrase: more than five words, or a number, or a question mark, or a tension word. 'Oldest Written Languages' is the failure; 'Why 3 of the 5 Oldest Scripts Are Still Unreadable' is the shape.

Every segment's TOPIC (a 2-4 word on-screen label) must share at least one real word with the TITLE — the gate checks a keyword bridge from each segment to the headline. Rename the topic, or write the title so it names what the segments are about.

Every NUMBER you say in a segment's SAY must be one that segment's data can show: a listed value, a difference between two of them, a percent change, a share of the total, or the same value in a bigger unit. A number from nowhere is refused — a guard derives every spoken quantity from the listed points.
Keep every number that is already correct. Do not add a country, company or person the data does not name.

PACE: each SAY is ONE spoken sentence of at most 16 words — the number and what it means, nothing else; the HOOK at most 14 words, the CLOSING at most 10, the QUESTION at most 8. A beat is on screen about 8 seconds; a longer line is refused. Each SAY says its beat's headline number out loud.
TOPIC labels are printed on the video: at most 4 words, no clause.

The HOOK is a 2000s download-site ad, not a fact read aloud: 6-14 words, the VIEWER is the one it happens to ('your coffee', 'your town'), lead with the shock, a visceral verb (wiped out, vanished, doubled, gone), one number from the data. Never a quiz ('Which animal...', 'Did you know...'), never a hedge (might, may, perhaps). Exaggerate the FEELING, never the FACT.

how_to_answer: Rewrite the WORDS so this story clears every rule above and answers every reason in `held_for`. Same number of segments, same order. Use ONLY numbers you can derive from each segment's `data.points` (or a year that appears as a label). If `judge` is present, its `problems`/`fixes` are what the video editor saw on the RENDERED video — shorter topics and one clear number per line are what fix 'unreadable' and 'text on text'. Write answer_path as one JSON object matching answer_schema, request_id and slug copied, and commit it. Do not touch the request.
